title: The Skybase Artifact is published with core token and legal parameters explicitly deferred to future iterations
content:
Chunk A.6.1.1.4.2.1 contains an unusual density of deliberate blanks. The Genesis Account address "will be specified in a future iteration of the Skybase Artifact" (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.1.3.1.1.4); so will the Development Company (…1.1.6), the SKYBASE Genesis Supply (…4.2.1.1.3), the token address (…4.2.1.1.4), the token Admin (…4.2.1.1.5), and the minting and initial distribution processes (…4.2.1.2).

The pattern is a design choice, not an oversight: each gap is a named document with an explicit deferral statement rather than an omission. The Artifact structure is therefore *complete* while its contents are partial, which lets the Agent exist, hold a SubProxy and a StarGuard, and operate an Accord before its token economics are settled.

This produces a genuine tension with A.6.1.1.4.2.1.4.2.1.1.6, which declares emissions above the Genesis Supply "permanently disabled" and irreversible by Skybase Governance. A permanent cap has been fixed relative to a quantity that has not yet been chosen — so the substantive dilution question is fully delegated to whoever later fills in the Genesis Supply, under the protection of an irrevocability clause that is already in force.

The general lesson: in this framework, irreversible commitments can be enacted before the values they bind are known, which shifts scrutiny from the commitment clause to the parameter-filling amendment that follows it.
description: Genesis Account, Development Company, Genesis Supply, token address and admin are all named placeholders — including a permanent emission cap set above a supply that does not yet have a number.
